summary.one_liner: A curated, link-only list of programming talks (mostly YouTube videos) organized by programming language and by theory topic, with runtimes, years and speaker names.
summary.what_it_does: The README is an "awesome"-style index of recommended conference talks rather than code. It has a "On Programming Languages" section with per-language subsections (for example Clojure, C++, Python, Haskell, Go, Erlang, Elixir, Ruby, Julia) and an "On theory" section with topics such as compilers, databases, distributed systems, type theory, testing and security. Each entry lists the talk title, approximate runtime, speaker and year. Some entries carry an [A] marker meaning someone judged the talk listenable as audio only. The author adds short notes on speakers and specific talks, and the README includes a list of favourite speakers. The list links out to external sites, mostly YouTube, and contributions are accepted by pull request.
use_cases: find conference talks on a specific programming language
discover talks on compilers, type theory or distributed systems
pick audio-friendly talks to listen to while commuting
browse talks on C++ performance or Clojure design
notable: Organized by language and by theory topic, with runtime and year for each talk
[A] marker flags talks that someone considered listenable as audio only
Author's notes on standout speakers and on talk quality or prerequisites
Multi-part talks and lecture series are grouped together under one heading
caveats: Links point to external sites, mostly YouTube; the author does not control the content and some links may go stale
